en.title: Benjamín Naishtat's 'Glaxo' Explores Argentina's Loss of Innocence on Global Stage
en.summary: Argentinian filmmaker Benjamín Naishtat's highly anticipated 'Glaxo' is set to captivate audiences at prestigious festivals. The film delves into profound themes of betrayal and memory, marking a significant moment for Latin American cinema.
en.body:
The cinematic landscape is abuzz with anticipation for **Benjamín Naishtat**'s latest offering, **‘Glaxo’**. Selected for both the Toronto International Film Festival and the San Sebastián International Film Festival, this Argentinian production is poised to be one of the year's most significant Latin American releases. Naishtat, known for his incisive explorations of power and societal unease, appears to be charting a course through the very fabric of a nation's collective consciousness.

Drawing parallels to literary giants like Mario Vargas Llosa, who questioned Peru's descent in "Conversation at The Cathedral," Naishtat's **‘Glaxo’** is described as an examination of Argentina's entire loss of innocence. This ambitious scope suggests a film that will grapple with themes of betrayal, guilt, and the enduring weight of memory. Naishtat, a graduate of Universidad del Cine and Le Fresnoy, has a distinguished festival pedigree, with previous works like **‘Historia del Miedo’**, **‘El Movimiento’**, and the San Sebastián Silver Shell-winning **‘Rojo’** premiering at major international events. His most recent collaboration, **‘Puan’** (co-directed with María Alché), garnered Best Screenplay at San Sebastián and a Goya nomination, further highlighting his critical acclaim.

## A Political Mirror for Our Times

Naishtat's cinema has consistently offered a critical lens on Argentina's past and present, often embedding these political undercurrents within compelling narrative frameworks. His ability to connect with audiences through genre—a skill evident in the success of **‘Rojo’**—suggests that **‘Glaxo’** will likely be both intellectually stimulating and viscerally engaging. The film's selection for premiering at two of the world's most respected film festivals underscores its potential to spark global conversations about impunity, power structures, and national identity. As Naishtat himself has hinted, the film aims to capture a specific, perhaps painful, historical moment.

## Global Stage, Local Truths

The international recognition of **‘Glaxo’** at festivals like Toronto and San Sebastián is a testament to the growing global appetite for diverse cinematic voices and narratives that challenge conventional storytelling. For fans of thoughtful, politically charged cinema, this film represents a crucial moment to engage with Naishtat's unique vision. The film's exploration of betrayal and guilt resonates universally, offering a mirror to societal fractures that extend far beyond Argentina's borders. The anticipation is palpable, with many eager to see how Naishtat translates these complex themes into a compelling cinematic experience that can resonate with a worldwide audience.

## What's Next

**‘Glaxo’** is slated for release in 2026, with its world premiere set to take place at the Toronto International Film Festival this week, followed by its San Sebastián debut. Further details regarding wider distribution and release dates are expected to be announced following its festival run.
